processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cylindrical specimen (φ 6 mm × 9 mm) cut along rolling direction; polished to facilitate thermocouple welding.

processing_steps.method: cooling to deformation temperature and soaking

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: First-stage hot compression at 1050 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹, deformed to fixed strain ε_I = 0.2.

processing_steps.method: hot compression with continuous temperature decrease
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Temperature continuously decreased from 1050 °C to 950 °C within the strain range 0.2–0.3 at a strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹.
Specimen compressed to final (total) strain ε_total = 0.9 at 950 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹.
Immediate water quenching to freeze the high-temperature microstructure morphology.

structures.overall_structure: Initial mixed-grain austenite microstructure (before deformation), used as the starting RVE for this sample

microstructure_list.region: representative areas 550 µm × 550 µm on different sections

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: SD 54.54 µm; Min 10.22 µm; Max 265.20 µm

structures.overall_structure: As-quenched martensitic microstructure reconstructed to prior austenite grains (PAGs); near-complete dynamic recrystallization

phases_present.phase_name: prior austenite grains (reconstructed from as-quenched martensite)

structures.overall_structure: 3D CA-simulated final microstructure at 0.9 strain for decreasing temperature 1050→950 °C with ε₁=0.2

measurement_conditions.environment: Gleeble 1500 thermomechanical simulator; tantalum foil (0.1 mm) between specimen ends and indenter
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Temperature ramped at 10 °C/s from 1050 °C to 950 °C over strain range 0.2–0.3; total strain 0.9; water quenched

stress_strain_curves.note: After the temperature drop, WH raises stress to a new second-stage peak lower than the constant 950 °C condition; stress then decreases briefly and later rises due to interfacial friction.

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure flow stress under varying (decreasing) temperature
characterization_methods.key_findings: Second-stage peak stress ≈70 MPa at ε≈0.3 (lower than constant 950 °C condition)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: sections ground with SiC papers, polished with 1 µm and 0.25 µm diamond pastes, etched with saturated picric acid solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe prior austenite grain (PAG) microstructure at the center of the side section and calculate equivalent grain diameter
characterization_methods.key_findings: PAG equivalent diameters measured; Image Pro Plus used for area-based equivalent diameter calculation

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SU5000 scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with an EBSD detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished with 10% perchlorate alcohol solution at 30 V and 0.25 A for 30 s; step size 0.65–1.3 µm
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize as-quenched martensitic microstructure and reconstruct prior austenite grains
characterization_methods.key_findings: Reconstructed PAG AGS 53.29 ± 3.77 µm and DRX fraction 96.1% at 0.9 strain for this sample

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ARPGE software (Greninger-Troiano orientation relationship); AZtecCrystal software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: GOS threshold defined at 3°; boundaries with misorientation >10° for PAG equivalent diameter
characterization_methods.purpose: Reconstruct prior austenite grains from EBSD and distinguish recrystallized grains from deformed ones
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX fraction 96.1% for decreasing 1050→950 °C, ε₁=0.2 sample at 0.9 strain

computational_details.simulation_method: Modified phenomenological constitutive model (Model 2) with varying t0.5 and stress softening coefficient k_s
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Under varying deformation conditions Model 2 gives RMSE 3.0399 MPa, R² 0.9507, AARE 3.11% (improved from Model 1: 6.4554 MPa, 0.8239, 7.36%).

analytical_models.equation_role: Characteristic stresses, DRX kinetics and softening coefficient used for this sample's simulation
analytical_models.model_note: Parameters optimized by genetic algorithm (GA); Model 2 modifies t0.5 and saturation stress via k_s for the second stage.

computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density and grain-boundary sliding (GBS)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: RVE 550 µm × 550 µm × 550 µm; cell size L0 = 2.5 µm; initial uniform dislocation density 10^11 m^-2; two-stage load condition 1050 °C (stage I, 0.01 s⁻¹) then decreasing to 950 °C over strain 0.2–0.3
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: 3D CA under varying conditions: flow stress RMSE 3.3118 MPa, R² 0.9589, AARE 4.57%; AGS RMSE 4.0169 µm, R² 0.9777, AARE 4.11%; DRX fraction RMSE 0.0229, R² 0.9784, AARE 2.47%.

analytical_models.equation_role: Dislocation-density evolution, GBS, nucleation and grain growth for this sample's CA simulation
analytical_models.model_note: C_drx, E, A_GB, H0 and P_GB solved by GA optimization; K, b, ν, δD_ob, n_GB, V_m, α_dis from literature.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: FEM validated the constitutive model against experimental load/stroke under varying conditions (Fig. 10).

unmapped_findings: For the decreasing-temperature (1050→950 °C) ε₁=0.2 sample at 0.9 strain, the reconstructed final PAG AGS (53.29 ± 3.77 µm, DRX 96.1%) is slightly larger than the constant 950 °C condition (52.01 ± 3.48 µm, DRX 97.2%) at nearly the same DRX fraction.

In the decreasing-temperature tests at 0.01 s⁻¹, the greater the strain at which the temperature starts to decrease, the lower the second-stage peak stress becomes; for ε₁=0.2 the second peak is ≈70 MPa while for ε₁=0.4 it is ≈66 MPa.

For this sample, after the temperature drop from 1050 °C to 950 °C within the 0.2–0.3 strain interval, the stress rises to a new peak lower than the constant 950 °C condition, then briefly decreases before a significant boost attributed to interfacial friction.
